title: Strictification of a birational group law over a field or trait
statement: Let $B$ be a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-weil-field, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. Let $X$ be a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme with nonempty fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An open in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if its intersection with each fibre is dense. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, up to equality on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Let $m:X\times_SX\dashrightarrow X$ be $S$-rational, associative wherever both composites are defined, such that $\Phi(x,y)=(x,m(x,y))$ and $\Psi(x,y)=(m(x,y),y)$ are $S$-birational. The law is called strict if there is an open $D\subseteq X\times_SX$ on which $m$ is defined and $\Phi,\Psi$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$, $D\simeq W$ onto open subschemes, with $D,V,W$ dense in every fibre of each projection $X\times_SX\to X$. There is a smooth separated finite-type $S$-dense open subscheme $X^\circ\subseteq X$ such that the restriction of $m$ to $X^\circ$ is strict. If $B$ is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$ and $m$ is defined on all of $X_F\times_FX_F$ and makes $X_F$ a group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], $X^\circ$ can be chosen to contain $X_F$.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Definition 1 and Proposition 2, printed pp.115-117 (PDF pp.121-123), including the generic-fibre preservation visible in the proof; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_SX$. It is smooth over $S$ by smooth base change and composition. Choose $S$-dense isomorphism charts for $\Phi$ and $\Psi$, and intersect their source opens with a representative domain for $m$. These representatives agree on their overlaps: their equality on an $S$-dense common open extends to the overlap by smooth fibrewise schematic density and uniqueness into a separated target. Restriction of an isomorphism to an open is an isomorphism onto an open, and a dense open in its source has dense image in its open target on each fibre. Thus we obtain one $S$-dense open $U\subseteq P$ on which $m$ is a morphism, and isomorphisms $\Phi:U\simeq V$ and $\Psi:U\simeq W$ onto $S$-dense opens of $P$. Set $Z=U\cap V\cap W$; a finite intersection of dense opens is dense on each fibre.

source.place: 5.2 Proposition 2, opening: common U, V, W and Z; 2.5 preliminaries

proof.text: Apply projection-density shrinking to $Z$. Choose its open $A\subseteq X$ and write $Q=A\times_SA$. For every $a\in A$, the opens $U,V,W$ restrict to dense opens in both $\{a\}\times_SX$ and $X\times_S\{a\}$, with $\{a\}=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(a)$. The inverse image of $A$ in each such fibre is also dense, by base change of smooth fibrewise density. Therefore these density statements remain true after imposing that the other coordinate belongs to $A$. All density arguments below can be made over $\kappa(a)$, making $a$ a rational point; no algebraic closure or geometric irreducibility is needed.

source.place: 5.2 Proposition 2, construction of X prime and reduction to a rational point a

proof.text: Define $U'=U\cap Q\cap(m|_U)^{-1}(A)$, $V'=\Phi(U')$ and $W'=\Psi(U')$. They are open in $Q$ and the two restricted maps are isomorphisms onto their images. Fix $a\in A$ and work over $\kappa(a)$. The slice $\Phi_a:U\cap(\{a\}\times_SX)\simeq V\cap(\{a\}\times_SX)$ is an isomorphism between dense opens of $X_{\kappa(a)}$, since $\Phi$ fixes the first coordinate. Intersect its source with the dense open $A_{\kappa(a)}$ and with the inverse image of $A_{\kappa(a)}$ in its target. The resulting dense open is precisely the first-projection fibre $U'_a$. The identical argument with $\Psi$, fixing the second coordinate, gives density of the second-projection fibres of $U'$. Their images under these slice isomorphisms show that $V'$ is first-projection dense and $W'$ is second-projection dense.

source.place: 5.2 Proposition 2, middle paragraph, four of the six density conditions

proof.text: For the remaining density of $W'$ over the first projection, fix $a\in A$, write $U^m_a=(m|_U)^{-1}(a)$, and set $V_a=V\cap(X\times_S\{a\})$, $W_a=W\cap(\{a\}\times_SX)$. The two isomorphisms restrict to $U^m_a\simeq V_a$ via $\Phi$ and $U^m_a\simeq W_a$ via $\Psi$. Both $V_a$ and $W_a$ are dense opens of $X_{\kappa(a)}$ by step 2. Their intersections with $A_{\kappa(a)}$ are dense. Pulling back these two dense opens to $U^m_a$ and intersecting gives a dense open; it is exactly $U^m_a\cap U'$, because its conditions are $x\in A$, $y\in A$, $m(x,y)=a\in A$. Its image under $\Psi$ is $W'\cap(\{a\}\times_SX)$, hence is dense in $W_a$ and therefore in $X_{\kappa(a)}$. Interchanging $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ proves that $V'$ is second-projection dense. Restricting to $A_{\kappa(a)}$ gives the required fibres of $Q$.

source.place: 5.2 Proposition 2, final paragraph, diagram through U_a and the two cross-density conditions

proof.text: Take $X^\circ=A$ and $D=U'$. Steps 3 and 4 establish all six projection-density conditions for $D,V',W'$. The associative identity is inherited on every domain where the restricted composites are defined, since those are composites of the original $m$. The open $A$ is smooth, separated, finite type and $S$-dense by step 2. Thus the restricted law has exactly the stated strictness properties.

In the additional trait case, choose the charts of step 1 to contain all of $P_F$. Indeed $m_F$ is a group law, and $\Phi_F^{-1}(x,z)=(x,x^{-1}z)$, $\Psi_F^{-1}(z,y)=(zy^{-1},y)$ are morphisms everywhere. Glue these isomorphisms over the open generic fibre to the chosen charts. On overlaps the maps and their inverses agree, by fibrewise schematic density and separated-target uniqueness as in step 1; their compositions are identities on each piece. The resulting isomorphism charts share a source containing $P_F$, so $U_F=V_F=W_F=P_F$ and $Z_F=P_F$. The preservation clause of projection-density shrinking now gives $A\supseteq X_F$. Repeating steps 3 and 4 with this choice proves the final assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-867ea7e8f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and the parent route in full. Statement unchanged: it matches the citer lem-sfb-trait-birational-group-envelope and the strictness definition in lem-sfb-strict-birational-law-realization. The item does not cite the realization node, so there is no cycle. BLR is not in literature/, so I could not open it; the delivery lists it as WANTED and marks the proof agent-written. Steps 1-6 check: step 1 uses clause (2) of lem-pc-proper-base-change (smooth base change of morphisms), smooth_comp, smooth fibrewise scheme-theoretic density on the open overlaps and separated-target uniqueness from lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated. Steps 3-4 are the six projection-density conditions, checked by hand through the slice isomorphisms, using m=p2∘Φ=p1∘Ψ for the two cross conditions. Step 5 assembles them; D is S-dense because Q_s→A_s is open. Step 6 glues Φ_F⁻¹=(x,x⁻¹z) and Ψ_F⁻¹=(zy⁻¹,y) on the open P_F; the charts preserve fibres, so the glued maps are isomorphisms. That gives Z_F=P_F, and the preservation clause of the shrinking node then gives A⊇X_F. New nodes are true. Smooth-fibrewise-dense: density survives field extension because the fibre map is open, and smooth fibres are reduced, so EGA IV 11.10.10 gives universal scheme-theoretic density. Projection-density-shrink: the bad locus E is constructible (EGA IV 9.5) and misses the generic points of the special fibre by flatness. Remove the two fibrewise closures; their dimensions are too small to swallow a component of X_s. If Z_F=P_F then E∩X_F is empty. Tested on empty X, zero-dimensional and disconnected X, and Z=P. Neither node has a duplicate: rg -L over the whole DAG found none, and Mathlib has no scheme-theoretic density notion. Tool uses accepted: lem-pc-proper-base-change clause (2), lem-trf-smooth-composition (Mathlib leaf) and lemma-nagata-ext, all generic. Batch-5 check: lem-trf-smooth-composition is the Mathlib leaf smooth_comp, a general tool with no proof deps, outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions, so the citation stands. No SGA. Maintainer note: blueprint.from.node is null, inherited from the ancestor chain; BLR is still WANTED.
